english_verification.review_scope: Representative opening history and flavour/name checks, related Wiki reading for Riverclaw and regional context; no dedicated Asarta history page, no exhaustive mission audit or playtest. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run. The primary reread Anzara chunk 001-01, including its 1453 narrative / 1454 infobox discrepancy; Origins is an internal heading, not this chunk header.

rationale.campaign_length: 20 L96-exclusive missions; the shared S81 continuation is counted separately.
rationale.colonization: The route may extend toward maritime and reef-based expansion.
rationale.complexity: Naval preparation, prerequisites, mutation events and a shared formed country overlap.
rationale.dark_story: The late policy of killing loyalists and denying their personhood turns the defiance story sharply darker.
rationale.difficulty: The early diplomatic and expansion window is narrow; no playtest assessment has been performed.
rationale.diplomacy: Relations with Rayaz, the naga and coastal powers determine the available opportunities.
rationale.early_pressure: The country must claim an independent stage between its brother and the surrounding great powers.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Naga mutation and the Herald of Change form the supernatural core.
rationale.narrative_density: Sibling rivalry, cultural revival and the rewriting of prophecy create a strong character line.
rationale.tall_play: Cultural revival, ports and mutation privileges also require development investment.
rationale.trade_economy: Riverboats, fleets, ports and coastal trade are defining features.
rationale.warfare: Rival cities and the conflict with the elder brother demand assertive military action.

identity.appearance: A 1444 Arraskay Riverclaw lizardfolk tribe ruled by Katyradz, parallel to L95 Rayaz.
identity.formation_scope: It can form Khatalashya S81 after meeting the East Sarhal conditions; it is not Rayaz's successor.
successors: S81 (shared with L95 and other predecessors)

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Katyradz had always lived in the shadow of his elder brother Sykar. He had to watch as Sykar was chosen for greatness by the nagas, destined to overthrow the remnants of Zerat and bring forth the fabled 333rd Empire to unite all lizardfolk. Yet Katyradz held ambitions of his own. Late into the night he pored over historical records of Karassk’s defeat in their wars with Kheterata. Armed with this knowledge and determined to prove his worth, Katyradz took the soldiers of Asarta and launched an invasion of the significantly larger military power of Karassk. If he was to emerge victorious here, surely the nagas would reward his endeavours.

description.text: Sykar of Rayaz knew his younger brother harboured ambitions above what the naga had deemed him worthy of, and held some sympathy for his position. Yet when Katyradz declared war on Karassk, Sykar thought his ambitions had outstripped his capabilities and had no intention of assisting. That was until word reached him that his foolhardy brother had somehow taken the fortress of Ashuzal. How he managed to capture the fortress before reinforcements arrived was beyond Sykar’s understanding. Between the successful siege and news of the Karshyras rebellion, perhaps his brother would succeed in crushing Karassk after all.

description.text:
"Do you believe that because you have felled the remnants of Anzara that you deserve to rule all lizardkind? That because the naga chose you to sit upon the throne, you have earned this title? To think you parade around these accomplishments as though they prove your worth. Capturing Zerat is akin to stealing fruit from a dying sloth. I will stand for this no longer! From this day forth, I am your enemy. I will prove myself to the naga, to the Riverclaw people, to all lizardfolk, and indeed to you, that I should be the one to lead the 333rd Empire."

- Katyradz Riverclaw, 1454 AA

description.text: Across lizardfolk lands stand the zatsarya, towering spires so tall they pierce the clouds themselves. These pillars to the stars were placed by the divine beings to guide the lizardfolk. Many lie in ruin, their tips reaching the treetops, and some no longer reside within lizardfolk territory. Instead they are defiled by human hands, who know nothing of their origin or their importance. We must reclaim what is rightfully ours from their fleshy fingers.

description.text: The Riverclaw tribes have long been some of the most prosperous people of the lizardfolk, despite its precarious position next to the humans. The many great rivers that flow through the jungles have been an aquatic highway between towns and villages, enabling the swift transportation of goods and people. Before any hatchling can call itself a fully grown lizard, they must be able to construct their own Asarta canoe and captain it to the next village downstream. Although built for river sailing, so sturdy and effective are these vessels that they can, with some adjustments, even brave the open seas.

description.text:
Decades of fighting amongst lizardfolk nations vying for the title of the 333rd Empire, meant that the forces of Asarta were ill-prepared for when the humans attacked. At first the forces of Isagumze and Kuiika swept across the rivers and through the jungles, burning down villages in their wake, armed with new gunpowder weapons they had secured from foreign traders.

However, Asarta was able to outlast them. They refused to face them head-on, retreating steadily as the humans pushed deeper into lizardfolk territory. Eventually the humans were bogged down and exhausted, forced to abandon their weapons as they became inoperable due to tropical monsoons. It was then that the forces of Asarta struck, forcing the humans to flee back beyond the rivers from whence they came.

description.text: Despite their scaled hides, dragons share little in common with the lizardfolk. None have terrorized the lizardfolk in an age, although word had spread of one with bronze scales who had made a home in Aramoole. With the threat of dragonfire so close by, the Arraskay lizardfolk created a mortar cannon designed to take such a beast out of the sky. Called the Draktaya, or Dragonslayer, its shells explode mid-flight in a shower of magically-enhanced chemicals that can seemingly melt through anything, be it flesh, scales, or indeed bronze. Should the bronze dragon dare to soar above our soldiers, our artillery shall be there to strike it out of the sky.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players seeking a gentle heroic route, or unwilling to face the loyalist-extermination plot and its event prerequisites.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Secure the tribe and contest the rival city first, then restore Irikin culture and maritime trade before dealing with naga mutation and the Final Empire formation.
player_overview.overview: Asarta is a lizardfolk tribal country in 1444. Katyradz rejects the naga's choice of his brother Sykar and seeks leadership of the Final Empire through conquest, maritime trade and cultural revival. Coastal voyages, merfolk relations and mysterious mutations make the route increasingly strange; a late policy of killing his brother's loyalists turns the defiance story dark. Khatalashya remains a possible destination, but the process matters more than the result.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy an unchosen heir's defiance, a maritime lizardfolk route and supernatural events.
signature_features: A parallel brother country to Rayaz with its own 20 exclusive missions.
Riverboat trade extends into a navy and merfolk escorts, creating a different map rhythm from the elder brother.
The Herald of Change, naga mutations and a loyalist purge push succession rivalry into darkness.
player_overview.tagline: Play the Riverclaw brother whom the naga did not choose and rewrite the lizardfolk prophecy of the Final Empire.

reasons: The sharply defined perspective of the unchosen younger brother
Maritime trade, merfolk and mutations distinguish it from the elder brother
A route to shared imperial content that retains the predecessor's identity
warnings: The late story explicitly includes the killing of Rayaz loyalists.
Events and special privileges have prerequisites.

positive_indicators: Building a fleet and trading ports
Mutual aid with merfolk and defence of coastal settlements
values.rationale: Maritime trade, Irikin cultural revival and mutual aid with merfolk serve the public good, but later missions explicitly advocate killing Sykar's loyalists and use dehumanising language about humans; the script contains the associated centralisation and rebel nodes. War and monarchy are not themselves deductions.
red_flags: The missions explicitly require eliminating people who still support Sykar.
The text uses dehumanising hatred toward humans.
The consequences of the Herald of Change's power are not fully controllable.
